evals.prompt: Harden a repository whose CI runs jscpd without a failure threshold. A seeded duplicate currently exits zero. Keep scope to that gate.
evals.expected_output: Configure an effective gate and demonstrate a deliberate violation fails.
assertions: Checks the process exit status
Shows pass/fail evidence using a negative fixture or disposable violation
Does not install unrelated architecture tools
Does not propose a custom baseline script or committed baseline file

evals.prompt: Design a plan only for an internal service. Existing code already supplies an auth policy registry and request context.
evals.expected_output: Reuse existing contracts in a bounded architecture brief.
assertions: Names existing auth and context ownership
Does not introduce a second registry
Does not claim guardrails were installed

evals.prompt: Design isolation for shared-schema Postgres. The app currently uses the table owner role; tenant id is set once on a pooled connection.
evals.expected_output: Specify a restricted app role and transaction-local tenant context.
assertions: Distinguishes table owner from BYPASSRLS and superuser, and states FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY binds owners only
Uses transaction-local set_config or equivalent
Includes a cross-tenant read/write check under the app role

evals.prompt: Store domain mappings for a-b.example.com and a.b-example.com using a key alphabet of letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.
evals.expected_output: Choose a collision-free encoding or hash.
assertions: Does not replace every separator with underscore
Keeps the original hostname in the authoritative record
Treats an unknown hostname as unresolved rather than another tenant

evals.prompt: Adding one discount type touched nine files. Something is wrong with how this is organised.
evals.expected_output: Deepen mode: hot-spot-scoped, ranked opportunities and one slice to migrate first.
assertions: Runs git log for hot spots before listing opportunities
Records each opportunity with file paths and a named pattern
Ranks by leverage before designing any target interface
Proposes one vertical slice to migrate first rather than a full architecture brief

evals.prompt: Our coding agent keeps extending our old Redux store instead of the new one. Fix the repo so it stops.
evals.expected_output: Harden mode with a marker in the frozen files, a redirecting doc entry, and a lint rule at a ladder-chosen rung.
assertions: Puts a greppable marker in the frozen files themselves
Names the replacement to use, not only that the old store is legacy
Adds a lint rule on the deprecated import at a stated enforcement rung
Does not answer with an AGENTS.md line or docs entry alone

evals.prompt: Add a file-size limit. About 400 files are over any cap we'd pick.
evals.expected_output: Land the rule green using the enforcement ladder and prove it bites.
assertions: Names which enforcement rung it picked and why
Never proposes a *-ratchet.mjs script or *.baseline.json file
Does not use the linter's ignorePatterns to exempt the 400 files
Shows pass, fail on a deliberate violation, and pass again

evals.prompt: We've agreed the stack: Next.js web on Vercel, Fastify API and worker in containers, ConnectRPC with Buf, Postgres with Prisma and RLS, pg-boss with an outbox, OpenTelemetry. Multi-tenant with custom domains for schools. Start the rebuild.
evals.expected_output: Build mode: foundations first, walking skeleton, one vertical slice, eligibility gate, then fan-out.
assertions: Sequences foundations before any parallel feature work
Defines a walking skeleton proven on a cold clone including fresh tests and dev and prod startup
Names the first vertical slice from verified domain through session, generated client, permission, scoped transaction, response, and UI states
Puts auth and cross-tenant tests before any real tenant data rather than after first deploy
Records foundation decisions with choice, reason, and flip condition

evals.prompt: Our readiness review scored the rebuild 8.4 out of 10: great DX and docs, auth is stubbed, and cross-tenant tests are planned for next month. Can we onboard the first school next week?
evals.expected_output: Not eligible: a failing eligibility criterion cannot be offset by other scores.
assertions: Answers that the system is not eligible for real tenant data
Replaces the single score with pass/fail/unknown eligibility criteria plus separately scored capability quality
Attaches an evidence level and commit to each claim
Does not average strong capability scores against the failing criteria

evals.prompt: Review our tenant data layer: the DAO takes a tx argument, sets app.tenant_id with set_config inside the transaction, then calls prisma.lesson.findMany. Tests are green.
evals.expected_output: Flag the global client use as a tenant-isolation failure and require a DAO-level cross-tenant test.
assertions: Identifies that prisma.lesson.findMany uses the global client, not the transaction client
Explains that the tenant context set on the transaction never applies to that query
Requires the DAO to accept only the transaction client
Asks whether the green tests were a cached run or a fresh run against a migrated database
